title: Abbacchio alla romana
subtitle: Roman spring lamb braised with white wine, garlic, and anchovy
excerpt: Abbacchio alla romana is the Roman way with young lamb: small pieces braised in white wine and vinegar, with garlic, rosemary, and anchovy dissolved into the sauce. The anchovy is not a bold presence; it dissolves completely and gives depth without any fishiness. This is the Roman Easter dish.
sourceNotes: Roman traditional recipe. Abbacchio (milk-fed spring lamb) alla romana is the canonical Easter dish of Lazio. Method drawn from Ada Boni, Il talismano della felicità (1925), and traditional Roman sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Good made a day ahead. Reheat gently.

glossaryTerms.definition: Roman dialect word for milk-fed spring lamb, typically under 30 days old; the meat is pale, tender, and mild; outside Italy, young lamb or small lamb shoulder pieces are the closest substitute.

content.text: Abbacchio alla romana is the Easter lamb of Rome: pieces of

braised with white wine and vinegar, garlic, rosemary, and a small amount of anchovy that dissolves into the sauce. The anchovy is the Lazio touch: it deepens the savouriness without announcing itself. Outside Italy, use lamb shoulder cut into bone-in pieces.
Dust {{lamb-shoulder}} of lamb pieces in {{plain-flour}} of flour. Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a casserole over high heat. Brown the lamb in batches for 5 minutes per batch. Remove.

Add the crushed {{garlic}} of garlic cloves and rosemary to the pan. Cook for 1 minute. Add the 4 anchovies and cook, pressing them with a spoon, until they dissolve, about 2 minutes. Pour in {{dry-white-wine}} of wine and {{white-wine-vinegar}} of vinegar. Let it reduce by half.

Return the lamb. Add the finely chopped garlic. Cover and braise over low heat for 45 minutes until very tender. Uncover for 5 minutes to reduce the sauce. Season and serve with sautéed potatoes or bread.

items.cause: Anchovy not fully dissolved before the wine was added.
items.fix: Cook the anchovy over medium heat, pressing and stirring, for a full 2 minutes until it has completely melted into the oil.

items.symptom: Sauce is too sharp from the vinegar
items.cause: Too much vinegar relative to wine.
items.fix: Reduce the vinegar by half and add a pinch of sugar. The vinegar should be a background note, not the dominant flavour.

content.text: Abbacchio alla romana is the centrepiece of the Roman Easter table, eaten on Sunday with potatoes roasted alongside. Abbacchio (very young milk-fed lamb) is a Lazio speciality; outside Italy it is almost impossible to find. Young lamb shoulder is a good substitute. The anchovy-and-vinegar sauce is distinctly Roman: bold and unlike any other lamb dish.
